newsitem.title: ITALY: MOTORCYCLING-DOOHAN MAKES IT FIVE IN A ROW IN ITALY.
newsitem.headline: MOTORCYCLING-DOOHAN MAKES IT FIVE IN A ROW IN ITALY.

text.p: Australian 500cc motorcycling world champion Michael Doohan won the Italian Grand Prix for the fourth year in a row on Sunday in a race that became a procession after his rivals made mistakes.
The win was in fact the Australian's fifth victory in a row at the Mugello racetrack north of Florence. The triple world champion won the San Marino GP here in 1993.
Italy's Luca Cadalora was second on a Yamaha, 10.056 seconds behind, and Japan's Nobuatsu Aoki was third on a Honda.
It was Doohan's third win in four races and left him comfortably in the lead in the championship standings with 95 points, ahead of Spanish team mate Alex Criville on 78.

Doohan, who secured his first pole position of the season on Saturday, made a cautious start and was back in fourth place after the first lap with Japanese Honda rider Tadayuki Okada leading and Criville a close second.
But the Australian threaded his way into the lead by the end of lap four and jostled with Okada for two more laps.
From the seventh he was in front to the finish.
Behind him, Criville went wide into a sand trap on the ninth lap and spent the rest of the race catching up. The Honda rider finished fourth.
Okada retired in the 12th lap after narrowly avoiding a fall and miraculously heaving himself back into the saddle.
